newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Yasser Arafat in Ireland for EU talks.
newsitem.headline: Yasser Arafat in Ireland for EU talks.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived on Tuesday in Ireland, the current EU president, to seek EU-bloc support for reviving the troubled 1993 peace agreement with Israel.
"I am coming to the chairmanship of the EU for continuing discussions," Arafat told reporters on arrival from Norway, the country which brokered the agreements.

Arafat drove straight to talks with Prime Minister John Bruton and Foreign Minister Dick Spring, who visited the Middle East this month to show EU concern at renewed violence and the slow pace of peace talks.
"We are meeting Prime Minister Bruton and Mr. Spring for talks to push forward the peace process," Arafat said.
Arafat said strongly worded EU statements, critical of Israel, had helped the peace process.
The Palestinian leader was having a working dinner with Bruton and Spring and was due to pay a courtesy call on President Mary Robinson on Wednesday.
